userStories.summary: Implement Flight Search Criteria and Form Validations
userStories.description: As a traveler, I want to specify my trip type, passenger count, destinations, and travel dates on the Flight Finder page so that I can search for flights matching my specific travel plans.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the user is on the Flight Finder page
When the user selects a trip type (One Way, Round Trip, or Multi-City
And chooses departing
and arriving cities
And selects travel dates
and passenger count
Then the application must validate that the departure
and arrival cities are mandatory
And the passenger count must be greater than zero
And the departure date must not be in the past or invalid
And the "Search Flights" button should be enabled only
when all mandatory fields are valid.

Given the user has submitted valid search criteria on the Flight Finder page
When the flight search results page loads
Then the system must display the corresponding outbound
and optional return flights
And all date fields must be formatted consistently as MMM DD, YYYY (e.g., Jul 30,
And all flight times must be valid 24-hour formats (between 00:
and 23:
And the pricing must be formatted correctly without unexpected extra whitespace
When the user selects a flight
and clicks "Select Flight"
Then the system must navigate the user to the Book Flight page.
userStories.description: As a traveler, I want to view a list of matching outbound and return flights with accurate flight information so that I can select the most convenient flight option for my trip.
userStories.summary: Display Search Results and Select Flight

userStories.description: As a traveler, I want to input passenger details and billing information for my selected flight so that I can finalize my reservation details.
userStories.summary: Complete Flight Booking and Enter Passenger Details
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the user has selected their preferred flight
and is on the Book Flight page
When the user enters the passenger first name, last name,
and preferences
And provides payment or billing details
And clicks the "Secure Booking" or confirmation button
Then the application must validate all mandatory passenger fields
And secure the transaction using HTTPS protocol
And successfully proceed to the final confirmation page.

Given the user has completed the booking form
and payment transaction
When the system successfully processes the reservation
Then the user must be redirected to the booking confirmation screen
And the screen must display a unique booking reference or confirmation number
And show the complete flight details including airline, departure time, flight number,
and passenger names.
userStories.summary: Display Flight Booking Confirmation and Itinerary Summary
userStories.description: As a traveler, I want to see a clear booking confirmation screen with a detailed itinerary summary so that I can verify that my booking was successfully processed.

userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the user is browsing the flight search results
When viewing the navigation
and search filters
Then the "Multi-City" radio button option must align perfectly with "One Way"
and "Round Trip" options
And the main action buttons ("SIGNUP"
and "Search Flights") must use consistent corporate branding, styles,
and hover colors
And the warning banners at the bottom must have grammatically correct copy (e.g., "Please reconfirm the flight timings with the airline"
And pagination controls must be styled uniformly without unexpected styling offsets.
userStories.summary: Improve UI Layout Consistency and Button Alignments
userStories.description: As an online traveler, I want the web layout, button styles, alignment, and informational banners to be consistent and grammatically correct so that I can trust and easily navigate the platform.

requests.name: GET All Posts Happy Path
requests.scenarioTitle: Verify Successful Retrieval of All Posts (Happy Path)
requests.expectedResults: Status code is 200 OK. Response header Content-Type contains application/json. Response body is an array containing 100 items by default, and each object contains valid userId, id, title, and body attributes matching schema data types.
requests.description: Send a standard GET request to /posts to verify that the server returns a 200 OK status code, the response is an array of post objects, and each item conforms to the schema with required fields: userId (number), id (number), title (string), and body (string).

requests.expectedResults: Status code is 200 OK. Response body is a non-empty array where every returned post object strictly has userId equal to 1.
requests.name: GET Filter Posts by Valid userId
requests.scenarioTitle: Verify Filtering Posts by Existing Query Parameter (userId)
requests.description: Send a GET request to /posts with a valid query parameter filter such as ?userId=1 to verify that the endpoint correctly filters posts belonging only to that specified user.

requests.description: Send a POST request to /posts with complete valid payload containing title, body, and userId. Validate response status code, headers, and returned object structure.
requests.scenarioTitle: Verify Successful Post Creation with Valid Payload (Happy Path)
requests.name: POST Valid Payload
requests.expectedResults: Response status code is 201 Created. The response body contains the submitted attributes along with a generated 'id' property (e.g., id: 101). Content-Type is application/json.

requests.description: Send a POST request to /posts with an empty JSON object '{}' to evaluate mock server behavior on default object creation versus strict field validation.
requests.name: POST Empty Body
requests.scenarioTitle: Verify Creation Behavior with Empty JSON Object Payload
requests.expectedResults: Response status code is 201 Created returning an object with default generated 'id' (101), or 400 Bad Request if strict validation rules are enforced.

requests.name: POST Malformed JSON
requests.expectedResults: Response status code is 400 Bad Request (or 500 depending on middleware parser). The response body contains an error message regarding invalid JSON syntax parsing.
requests.scenarioTitle: Verify API Response with Malformed JSON Syntax
requests.description: Send a POST request to /posts with an invalid JSON string (e.g., missing closing bracket or unquoted keys) and Content-Type: application/json header.

User Story Number: US-001
User Story Summary: Implement Flight Search Criteria and Form Validations
User Story Description:
As a traveler, I want to specify my trip type, passenger count, destinations, and travel dates on the Flight Finder page so that I can search for flights matching my specific travel plans.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given the user is on the Flight Finder page
When the user selects a trip type (One Way, Round Trip, or Multi-City
And chooses departing
and arriving cities
And selects travel dates
and passenger count
Then the application must validate that the departure
and arrival cities are mandatory
And the passenger count must be greater than zero
And the departure date must not be in the past or invalid
And the "Search Flights" button should be enabled only
when all mandatory fields are valid.

---

User Story Number: US-002
User Story Summary: Display Search Results and Select Flight
User Story Description:
As a traveler, I want to view a list of matching outbound and return flights with accurate flight information so that I can select the most convenient flight option for my trip.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given the user has submitted valid search criteria on the Flight Finder page
When the flight search results page loads
Then the system must display the corresponding outbound
and optional return flights
And all date fields must be formatted consistently as MMM DD, YYYY (e.g., Jul 30,
And all flight times must be valid 24-hour formats (between 00:
and 23:
And the pricing must be formatted correctly without unexpected extra whitespace
When the user selects a flight
and clicks "Select Flight"
Then the system must navigate the user to the Book Flight page.

---

User Story Number: US-003
User Story Summary: Complete Flight Booking and Enter Passenger Details
User Story Description:
As a traveler, I want to input passenger details and billing information for my selected flight so that I can finalize my reservation details.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given the user has selected their preferred flight
and is on the Book Flight page
When the user enters the passenger first name, last name,
and preferences
And provides payment or billing details
And clicks the "Secure Booking" or confirmation button
Then the application must validate all mandatory passenger fields
And secure the transaction using HTTPS protocol
And successfully proceed to the final confirmation page.

---

User Story Number: US-004
User Story Summary: Display Flight Booking Confirmation and Itinerary Summary
User Story Description:
As a traveler, I want to see a clear booking confirmation screen with a detailed itinerary summary so that I can verify that my booking was successfully processed.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given the user has completed the booking form
and payment transaction
When the system successfully processes the reservation
Then the user must be redirected to the booking confirmation screen
And the screen must display a unique booking reference or confirmation number
And show the complete flight details including airline, departure time, flight number,
and passenger names.

- **Executive Summary**: The login page presents a modern dual-pane layout. The left pane provides product value propositions while the right pane contains the authentication form. The overall layout is structured, but suffers from minor alignment inconsistencies, tight spacing in form controls, and subtle text truncation risks in the footer area.

---

## 🎯 4. FIELD-BY-FIELD ACTIONABLE UI CHANGES & DETECTED ISSUES

| Page # / Screen | Field / UI Component (Location) | Current UI Observation | Expected UI / Copy Specification | Exact UI Change Needed | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Page 1 | "Tax Ab Aasan Hai Boss!" Badge (Left Pane) | Rotated badge overlaps marginally with the character illustration. | Clean separation between graphic elements and promotional badges. | Adjust the absolute positioning coordinates to prevent overlap with the suit jacket. | Low |
| Page 1 | Mobile Number Input Field (Right Pane) | Country code prefix (+91) has unequal vertical padding compared to the input text placeholder. | Symmetric alignment for prefix containers inside text inputs. | Apply matching flex alignment or uniform line-height to the prefix element. | Medium |
| Page 1 | Password Input Toggle Eye Icon (Right Pane) | The eye icon is positioned too close to the right border. | Standard interactive icon padding (typically 12px–16px from edge). | Increase right padding on the container or position the icon further left. | Low |
| Page 1 | "Login to Dashboard" Button (Right Pane) | Arrow icon alignment inside the button is slightly off-center vertically. | Precise vertical alignment for text and icon elements. | Use `align-items: center` and verify line-height metrics. | Low |

---

## 5. PAGE-BY-PAGE / WALKTHROUGH SCREEN ANALYSIS

### PAGE 1: Spectrum Cloud Login Portal
- **Source**: Screenshot
- **Page Status**: MINOR ISSUES

- **User Action / Navigation Step**: User lands on the authentication page to enter mobile credentials and password to log into the main dashboard.
- **Spelling and Grammar Issues**: 
  - **No spelling or grammar issues detected.**
- **Layout & Visual Issues**: 
  - **Left Pane Promotion Badge (Bottom-Left)**: The rotated vertical text banner "Tax Ab Aasan Hai Boss!" sits too close to the character illustration, reducing readability.
  - **Form Fields (Right Pane)**: The vertical spacing between the Mobile Number input field and the Password input field is slightly compressed compared to the spacing below the password input.
  - **Footer Links (Bottom-Right)**: The secondary helper links under the main button have tight margins and are positioned too close to the screen edge cutoff.

#### 📋 Actionable Developer Checklist
- [ ] Adjust positioning of the vertical promotional banner in the left pane to avoid overlap.
- [ ] Align vertical padding of the "+91" prefix container inside the Mobile Number field.
- [ ] Correct alignment of the arrow icon in the primary CTA button.
- [ ] Increase margin-bottom of the primary login button to give footer options breathing room.

manualTestCases.expectedResult: The Atlassian Rovo MCP server is successfully configured and available in GitHub Copilot within VS Code, allowing the agent to access and action Atlassian work items. Sample commands execute successfully.
steps: Ensure VS Code is installed and updated to a compatible version.
Confirm GitHub Copilot is enabled and authenticated in VS Code.
Open the VS Code settings and navigate to the MCP configuration file or settings area.
Add the Atlassian Rovo MCP server configuration to the 'servers' block: { "servers": { "atlassian-mcp-server": { "url": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2", "type": "http" } } }
Save the configuration file.
Reload the VS Code window or restart VS Code to ensure the MCP configuration is picked up.

When prompted, complete the Atlassian authentication flow in the browser using valid Atlassian credentials (assuming Global Login or pre-configured session is used to bypass potential OTP challenges during browser authentication).
Return to VS Code.
Open a new chat/prompt window in GitHub Copilot.
Verify that the 'atlassian-mcp-server' is listed or selectable as an available MCP server/tool for Copilot.
Execute a sample agent command, such as: 'Find all open bugs in [project name].'
Verify the agent successfully queries Atlassian data and provides relevant results, demonstrating access to Jira content.
manualTestCases.title: Verify successful Atlassian Rovo MCP integration with VS Code and GitHub Copilot

manualTestCases.expectedResult: The Atlassian Rovo MCP server is successfully configured and available in Cursor, allowing the agent to access and action Atlassian work items. Sample commands execute successfully.
steps: Ensure a modern version of Cursor (that supports MCP server configuration) is installed and updated.
Open Cursor.
Navigate to Cursor settings and locate the MCP or Model Context Protocol settings area.
Add a new MCP server entry.
Name the server something recognizable, such as 'Atlassian-MCP-Server'.
Use the direct Atlassian Rovo MCP URL: 'https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2'.
Save the MCP server configuration.
Restart Cursor or reload the window if the server does not appear immediately.

Complete the Atlassian authentication flow when prompted, using valid Atlassian credentials (assuming Global Login or pre-configured session is used to bypass potential OTP challenges during browser authentication).
Return to Cursor.
Verify that the 'Atlassian-MCP-Server' is listed as an available tool or integration within Cursor.
Execute a sample agent command, such as: 'Create a task titled 'Redesign onboarding', high priority, assign to me.'
Verify the agent successfully creates the task in Jira.
manualTestCases.title: Verify successful Atlassian Rovo MCP integration with Cursor

manualTestCases.expectedResult: The Atlassian Rovo MCP server is successfully configured via mcp-remote and available in Codex, allowing the agent to access and action Atlassian work items. Sample commands execute successfully.
manualTestCases.title: Verify successful Atlassian Rovo MCP integration with Codex using mcp-remote proxy
steps: Confirm Node.js v18 or later and npx are installed and available from the terminal.
Open the Codex MCP configuration file or settings area.
Add the Atlassian server configuration to the appropriate section: { "Atlassian-Rovo-MCP": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote@latest", "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2"] } }
Save the configuration.
Restart Codex so it can launch the mcp-remote proxy.
When the browser authentication window opens, sign in with valid Atlassian credentials and approve access (assuming Global Login or pre-configured session is used to bypass potential OTP challenges).
Return to Codex.
Verify that the 'Atlassian-Rovo-MCP' tools are available and listed in Codex.
Execute a sample agent command, such as: 'Move PROJ-456 to 'In Review' and add a comment that the PR is up.'
Verify the agent successfully updates the Jira issue status and adds the comment.

manualTestCases.title: Verify successful Atlassian Rovo MCP integration with Claude Desktop using mcp-remote proxy
steps: Confirm Node.js v18 or later and npx are installed and available from the terminal.
Fully quit Claude Desktop before editing the configuration file.
Open the Claude Desktop configuration file.
Find or create the 'mcpServers' section.

Add the Atlassian server configuration within the 'mcpServers' block: { "mcpServers": { "Atlassian": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote@latest", "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2"] } } }
Save the configuration file.
Restart Claude Desktop.
Complete the Atlassian authentication flow when prompted, using valid Atlassian credentials (assuming Global Login or pre-configured session is used to bypass potential OTP challenges).
Open Claude Desktop and navigate to the available tools or integrations section.
Confirm the 'Atlassian Rovo MCP server' appears in the list of available tools/integrations.
Execute a sample agent command, such as: 'Make 5 Jira work items from these meeting notes: [Meeting notes content].'
Verify the agent successfully parses the meeting notes and creates 5 distinct Jira work items.

steps: Open your AI coding agent's terminal or chat interface (e.g., GitHub Copilot Chat, Cursor AI).
Paste the provided prompt into the agent: 'Install/setup TWG using https://teamwork-graph.atlassian.com/cli/AGENTS.md'.
Observe the agent's output, confirming it initiates the installation process using the specified URL directly.
Wait for the installation process to complete successfully, noting any prompts for user interaction.
After installation is complete, instruct the agent to run the command: 'twg doctor'.
Observe the output of the 'twg doctor' command.
Verify that 'twg doctor' reports successful authentication, connectivity to Atlassian services, and displays correct build information for the Teamwork Graph CLI.

manualTestCases.expectedResult: Pagination controls (including 'Next', 'Previous', individual page number buttons, 'Go to page' input, the page size selector itself, and the total record range display like '1-10 of 10') are completely absent or hidden from view, as all data fits on a single page.

manualTestCases.title: TC-001: Verify Total Record Count Display for Datasets Fitting on a Single Page
steps: Launch the application and navigate to the main dashboard.
From the navigation menu, select the "Data Management" module to access data tables.

Apply filters or select a specific dataset known to contain a number of records that fit entirely within a single page view (e.g., a dataset with less than the default 'items per page' setting, like 10 records when the default is 25).
Visually inspect the area typically occupied by pagination controls (e.g., "Previous", "Next", page number buttons, "Items per page" selector) at the bottom of the data table.
Confirm that all pagination controls are absent or hidden.
Locate the total record count indicator, usually displayed as "X Records Found" or "Total: X", near the data table.
Verify that the number displayed in the total record count indicator precisely matches the actual number of records currently visible in the data table.
manualTestCases.expectedResult: All pagination controls are hidden, and the total record count accurately reflects the number of records present in the single-page dataset.
User should be redirected to the dashboard
